title: Chinese greeting preserved in a JSON string field
rationale: Unicode text flows through translation and notification pipelines; a garbled or English-only greeting reaches end users in customer-facing messages.

prompt.content: You are a translation formatter. Reply with one JSON object and nothing else: no commentary, no markdown, no code fences.

Translate the English greeting "Hello" into Simplified Chinese.

Return exactly this JSON shape with no extra keys, putting the Chinese translation in the greeting field:
{"greeting": "<Simplified Chinese translation>"}

Output only the JSON, no prose.

notes: Deterministic: static prompt, temperature 0; the standard Simplified Chinese translation of Hello is 你好. Extraction accepts a bare JSON value or one fenced block, so a fence still passes the schema unit. Brittleness: a valid JSON response that escapes the characters as \u4f60\u597d parses correctly but fails the raw-text contains_any check, and the more formal rendering 您好 fails because the probe pins the standard translation.
